title: openai-v1-param-normalizer-stable-stream-sentinel-and-toolcall-metadata
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Stabilizes /v1/chat.completions compatibility: parameter normalization (string vs array stops), consistent role aliasing, normalized logprobs/stop handling, streaming sentinel to reduce truncated frames, and explicit toolcall metadata attachment to structured outputs.
body:
Context and motivation:
This PR finishes a compatibility and robustness pass for the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer. We saw several customer integration issues where legacy clients sent stop as a string, roles were aliased, or streaming fragments caused partial toolcall objects to be emitted which broke downstream JSON parsers. The goal is twofold: 1) normalize parameter shapes to be forgiving and predictable, and 2) harden the streaming path so structured outputs (especially tool/function calls and JSON-enveloped responses) are emitted atomically or annotated with sentinel frames that allow consumers to reassemble safely.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Parameter normalizer: accept stop as single string or array, coerce to canonical array; normalize temperature/top_p bounds and coerce numeric-like strings into numbers when safe; provide a single canonical param map passed into the runtime.
- Role alias mapping: map common role aliases (assistant, system, user, system_prompt) into canonical roles so downstream model routing and safety checks are stable.
- Stop/logprob harmonization: ensure stop tokens are applied consistently across response scoring code and that logprob envelopes in streaming partials always include a final reconciliation message with global logprob delta when tokenization spans a fragment boundary.
- Streaming sentinel framing: introduce a lightweight sentinel frame ("sentinel:frame_end" metadata) emitted whenever a structured object (JSON block or toolcall) completes. This reduces cases where parser UIs see truncated JSON mid-stream. Sentinels are opt-in via header X-Redwood-Stream-Sentinels and default to enabled for /v1 compatibility routes.
- Toolcall metadata envelope: attach a stable metadata block to toolcall outputs: {"tool_name","confidence","schema_version"} as a final frame (or as part of the sentinel) so consumers can validate and decide whether to call the external tool or buffer.
- Backcompat shims: compatibility shim in the adapter layer to honor older client shapes (roles placed in messages[].role or messages[].author) and to translate them into the unified request object used by the runtime.

Why this is different from prior PRs:
Previous PRs focused on stream framing and stop semantics in isolation. This change stitches together parameter shape normalization, role aliasing, and a sentinel/meta strategy so that structured responses and toolcalls are both stable and backwards-compatible.

Checklist:
- [x] Canonical param mapping implemented and unit-tested (normalize(), sanitizeStop())
- [x] Streaming sentinel frames added and gated behind header toggle
- [x] Toolcall metadata envelope added to structured outputs
- [x] E2E integration tests for a) single string stops b) array stops c) fragmented JSON toolcall d) role aliasing scenarios
- [x] Docs updates and migration note for customers

Implementation notes:
- The normalizer lives in packages/api-adapter/src/param_normalizer.ts and exposes a single function normalizeOpenAIv1Params(request) -> { canonicalParams, warnings }. Warnings surface deprecated shapes as telemetry but do not fail requests.
- Streaming path change is limited to packages/streaming/src/framer.ts: we add an optional sentinel emission right after we transition from in-object to out-of-object when emitting a JSON/structured block. To keep latency low, the sentinel is a single 7-byte frame and is serialized only when X-Redwood-Stream-Sentinels=true.
- Toolcall changes in packages/response-formatter add a final metadata frame in the same encryption/serialization envelope as the last token to preserve atomicity.

Testing and validation:
- Unit: param_normalizer unit suite covers 18 cases across stop shapes and numeric coercion.
- Integration: e2e suite runs in CI with a simulated streaming consumer that asserts that every toolcall JSON block is followed by a sentinel or finalization event.
- Load: smoke load test (small cluster) to ensure sentinel emission does not degrade throughput; observed <1% p99 latency change.

Rollout plan:
- Deploy to main with feature flag enabled only for the /v1 compatibility route.
- Canary: 10% traffic for 24h, monitor structured-output parsing errors in Sentry plus message-level sanity metrics.
- Expand to 50% after 24h if no regressions, then 100%. Revert plan in place if parsing errors exceed the threshold defined in ENG-4219.

Compatibility and migration notes for customers:
- If you rely on receiving partial JSON without sentinel frames, set X-Redwood-Stream-Sentinels=false in your requests to retain previous behavior (not recommended).
- Clients that submit stop as a string will continue to work; we will emit a telemetry warning suggesting migration to arrays.
- Tooling that inspects logprob envelopes should consume the final reconciliation frame to get consistent probabilities across fragment boundaries.

Related work:
- Builds on streaming refactors in ENG-3890 and the initial /v1 adapter introduced in ENG-3511. See linked Linear tickets for follow-ups.

Ava Martinez (author): Addressed both nits — added benchmark and moved sentinel size to constants. PTAL.
